entries.title: Matthew 17:1
segments: Six days. After Peter's confession.  Luke says 'about eight days after' (

).  This would be according to the Jewish custom whereby each part of a day is counted as a day.
 

 
A high mountain apart. Probably Mount Hermon, near Caesarea Philippi.  It is 9,000 feet high.

entries.title: Matthew 17:3
segments: Moses and Elijah. The law and the prophets were represented in these two.

entries.title: Matthew 17:5
segments: Hear ye him. A command to hear and obey Jesus the Christ, the Son of God, rather than the law and the prophets.  The old dispensation and given place to the new.

entries.title: Matthew 17:9
segments:
Tell the vision to no man. The vision, literally, the thing seen.  Peter, James, and John were chosen to see the glory of Christ because they were the most spiritually enlightened of the apostles.  The others were not advanced enough, while the multitudes, if told of the glory on the mountain, would have tried to make Christ their earthly king.
 

 
Risen from the dead. The resurrection distinctly foretold.

entries.title: Matthew 17:15
segments: Epileptic. Jesus healed the epileptic immediately after coming down from the mountain of transfiguration.  He thus set the example of refusing to permit even the most exalted spiritual enjoyments to delay attention to duty.

entries.title: Matthew 17:16
segments: Thy disciples. The nine apostles were among them, the other three having been with Jesus on the mountain.

entries.title: Matthew 17:20
segments:
If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed. That is, the smallest degree of faith, which like the mustard seed is living and capable of great growth.
 

 
Ye shall say unto this mountain, etc.  Jesus employs this strong proverbial expression to illustrate the tremendous importance of faith (

entries.title: Matthew 17:23
segments: They were exceeding sorry. The disciples, not yet fully understanding the meaning of Christ's foretold death and resurrection easily fell into despondency over the prospect of losing his affectionate guidance and protection.  Three of them, Peter, James and John, who had witnessed the transfiguration, may have gained from it an idea of Christ's glory and power which enabled them to think of the resurrection hopefully; but the others were probably without this consolation.

entries.title: Matthew 17:24
segments: They that received the half-shekel. Officers of the Jewish authorities, whose duty it was to collect the annual tax for the support of the Temple services.  Every male Jew above twenty years of age had to pay the half-shekel, whose value was about thirty or thirty-five cents.  Jesus had been absent from Capernaum for some time and the tax was overdue.

entries.title: Matthew 17:26
segments: The sons are free. Meaning, the Son of God is rightly free from a tax for the services of his Father's temple.

entries.title: Matthew 17:27
segments: Lest we cause them to stumble. That is, lest a wrong impression of the unwillingness of Jesus to pay the tax should be made.
